canonicalExplanation.summary: A React app starts by giving React **one DOM element** to manage: `createRoot(document.getElementById("root")).render(<App />)`. From then on React **owns everything inside that container**. Your components describe what should be there, and React updates the real DOM to match, changing only what differs. Everything **outside** the container, like a server-rendered header or footer, stays yours. You call `render` once at startup; later updates come from state changes, not from calling render again.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
You're adding React to an existing course page. The header, navigation and footer are plain HTML, and only the "practice" area should be interactive. You worry React will wipe the whole page or add a second copy of the app every time something changes. createRoot(container).render() gives React ownership of the app container without replacing unrelated page landmarks. In this lesson you'll create and explain a minimal React root and component tree. ```predict {"question": "The page has `

examples.title: Handing React one container
examples.situation: createRoot(container).render(<App />) gives React ownership of the practice container without replacing unrelated page landmarks.
walkthrough: **Create the root:** `createRoot(container).render(<App />)` runs once when the page loads.
**Check the page:** DevTools will show header and footer unchanged, and App's section inside #practice.
examples.result: The practice area is interactive while the header, navigation and footer keep working as plain HTML.

examples.title: The app that appeared twice
examples.situation: A developer calls `createRoot(container).render(<App />)` inside a button click handler to "refresh" the app, and a warning appears about creating a root on a container that already has one.
walkthrough: The root was created again for the same container.
Each root should be created once at startup.
Fix: create the root once, and refresh by changing state inside App.
examples.result: The app has one root, and clicking the button updates it through state with no warnings.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Calling render appends a fresh duplicate DOM tree on every state change.
misconceptions.correction: State changes don't call render again, and React never appends a second tree. It compares the new description with the previous one and updates the same DOM nodes in place.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In the "No duplicates" predict, how many copies of App existed?

analogy.example: A React root is like **renting one shop unit in a mall**. Inside your unit (the container) you can rearrange everything; React is your shop manager. The corridors, other shops and signs (header, footer) belong to the mall and stay as they are.
limitations: Shops don't redraw themselves; React updates the unit when state changes.
You don't rent the unit again to rearrange it.

recap.summary: To create and explain a minimal React root, pick one container, call createRoot(container).render(<App />) once at startup, and let components describe the tree inside it. React owns only that subtree and updates it in place when state changes, never appending duplicates.
